facts.statement: Pepesuchus lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the state of São Paulo, Brazil.
facts.quote: It is a peirosaurid which lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now state of São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus was named by a team of researchers including Diogenes A. Campos and Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2011.
facts.quote: Pepesuchus was named by Diogenes A. Campos, Gustavo R. Oliveira, Rodrigo G. Figueiredo, Douglas Riff, Sergio A.K. Azevedo, Luciana B. Carvalho and Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2011

facts.statement: The genus name Pepesuchus honors Professor José Martin Suárez, nicknamed "Pepe", and combines it with the Greek word for crocodile.
facts.quote: The generic name honours Professor José Martin Suárez (known by his colleagues as "Pepe"), and "suchus", from Greek meaning crocodile.

facts.statement: The species name deiseae honors the paleontologist Deise Dias Rêgo Henriques.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the paleontologist Deise Dias Rêgo Henriques.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus had a roughly triangular skull covered in small pits when viewed from above.
facts.quote: The skull of Pepesuchus is roughly triangular when viewed from above and is covered in small pits.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus jaws were lined with many small, pointed teeth.
facts.quote: The jaws are lined with many small pointed teeth.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus possessed ziphodont teeth that were laterally compressed and serrated.
facts.quote: Like other sebecians, Pepesuchus has ziphodont teeth that are laterally compressed and serrated.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus had 17 teeth in each maxilla, which is the highest count among sebecians after Stolokrosuchus.
facts.quote: A total of 17 teeth are present in each maxilla, the most of any sebecian after Stolokrosuchus.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus is classified with the peirosaurids Peirosaurus, Lomasuchus, and Uberabasuchus based on shared characteristics.
facts.quote: Pepesuchus is united with the peirosaurids Peirosaurus, Lomasuchus, and Uberabasuchus on the basis of several shared characteristics.

facts.statement: Pepesuchus belongs to the parent group Pepesuchinae.
Pepesuchus is classified within the family Peirosauridae.
Pepesuchus lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Pepesuchus had a snout that was somewhat wider than those of other peirosaurids and curved slightly upward.
rejected.quote: The snout of Pepesuchus is somewhat wider than those of other peirosaurids and has a slight upward curve.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'somewhat wider than those of other peirosaurids and'

rejected.statement: Pepesuchus shares a ridge on the maxillary shelf of the palate with all members of the clade Sebecia.
rejected.quote: Pepesuchus also has a ridge on the maxillary shelf of the palate, a feature it shares with all members of the larger clade Sebecia (which includes peirosaurids and the related family Sebecidae).
